title: Pilot Elicitation Templates & Seller Scripts — sketch
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a lightweight, seller-facing playlet intended for fast pilot elicitation conversations with engineering/platform teams. Focus: capture technical constraints, success metrics, and data handling needs quickly so SEs can scope a minimal, low-friction pilot that proves value in 2–6 weeks.

Notes to self / usage guidance:
- Use as an accompaniment to a 30–45 minute technical discovery call.
- Pick 3–5 questions from each section depending on time.
- The goal of the initial call is to leave with a clear MVP pilot plan: inputs, expected outputs, evaluation set, run cadence, and a rough performance SLA.
- Keep conversation outcome-oriented (what will change if the pilot succeeds).

One-line intro script for sellers (30s):
- "Goal for today: understand your integration surface and success signal so we can propose a 2–6 week pilot that demonstrates measurable impact with low operational lift."

Opening framing questions (5–7 minutes)
- What product/feature are you trying to prototype or improve with LLMs? (single-sentence summary)
- Who are the consumers of the output (end users, other services, agents)? Any compliance constraints?
- What does success look like in 4–6 weeks? (quantitative if possible)
  - e.g., reduce triage time by X%, increase task completion by Y%, N converted leads, N saved agent-hours

Data & security quick probe (3–5 minutes)
- Are the inputs customer data, internal docs, or public text? Any PHI/PCI-sensitive fields?
- Does data need to remain in your VPC/on-prem or can it traverse an external API?
- Retention limits: Do you need logs disabled or truncated?
- Encryption/KMS needs? (bring up Redwood Private/Dedicated as options)

Integration surface & traffic profile (5–8 minutes)
- How will requests enter the system? (frontend, backend job, async queue, webhook)
- Typical request size and expected tokens per request (short example payload helps)
- Expected traffic shape: calls/sec peak and steady, bursts, concurrency targets
- Acceptable latency envelope for the pilot (p95 target, e.g., < 300ms, < 1s)

Quality & evaluation plan (5–10 minutes)
- What evaluation set can you provide? (sample of 50–200 representative examples ideal for pilot)
- Key metrics we should track: accuracy/precision, ROUGE/F1, human-rated quality, hallucination rate, latency, cost per request
- Who will do label/triage work if we need human-in-the-loop checks?

Operational & fallback considerations (3–5 minutes)
- What happens when model output is wrong/unavailable? (fallback to cache, simpler heuristic, human review)
- Acceptable error modes vs. show-stoppers (e.g., PII leakage is a show-stopper)

Pilot structure template (deliverable to circulate after call)
- Duration: 3–6 weeks
- Objectives: 1–3 measurable goals
- Data: sample set + access method (S3, POST endpoint, SQL export)
- Integration: SDK vs REST vs async batch
- Acceptance criteria: numeric thresholds + qualitative sign-off owners
- Rollout plan: single-team beta -> expand

Minimal viable pilot options (pick one based on risk appetite)
- Quick interactive demo (hosted API): low cost, fastest feedback. Best if no regulated data and latency tolerances moderate.
- Dedicated pool POC: reserved capacity for predictable p95 latency; pick if steady traffic and strict SLOs.
- Private (VPC) trial: needs security/compliance and customer-managed networking.

Seller conversation scripts (snippet bank)
- If customer cites latency concerns: "We can stage a dedicated pool with p95 latency guardrails for the pilot and instrument per-request traces so you can validate consistency before commit."
- If customer raises compliance: "We can propose a Private deployment sketch — we take a hybrid approach: control plane in Redwood, data path fully in your VPC or on-prem."
- If they want cost predictability: "We’ll model expected tokens using your sample set and show projected cost ranges for hosted vs dedicated. We can also propose caching to cut per-token spend."

Quick checklists for SE handoff (post-call)
- Send pilot one-pager within 48 hours that includes: objective, metrics, sample data sketch, proposed config (model family, quantization, batch settings), basic SLOs.
- Create a temporary tracking ticket (Jira) and link Confluence pilot page + evaluation rubric.
- Schedule a kickoff session with infra/ops contact for network/firewall checks if Private/Dedicated is chosen.

Examples of short evaluation rubrics (copyable)
- Metric: response relevance (0–3 scale) — target >= 85% of responses score 2 or 3 over 200 samples
- Metric: p95 latency — target <= 750ms under pilot concurrency
- Metric: cost per 1k requests — target <$X (use sample token calc table)

Unresolved questions to surface (notes for seller)
- Can they provide a 50–200 sample export by X date? If not, can SE use synthetic prompts to bootstrap?
- Is there an internal owner for privacy sign-off? Name and timeline?
- Are there existing rate-limiting or proxy layers that will affect token counting or latency?

Attachments & templates to send after call (quick links)
- Pilot one-pager template (copy-paste)
- Sample token calculator sheet (we use this to estimate cost ranges)
- Evaluation rubric template

Draft email to circulate post-call (copyable):
"Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Attached is a short pilot one-pager outlining our proposed 4-week trial, the evaluation rubric we discussed, and a request for a sample dataset (50–200 records) to get started. Next step: internal kickoff with your infra contact to validate network requirements. Please let me know who that is and availability for a 30-minute slot later this week."

Slack & ticket pointers (internal ops)
- Post pilot start notes in #pilot-ops with tags: @se @solutions-eng @platform-seller
- Create Jira ticket with component=pilot and label=pilot-elicitation; link to Confluence page and attach sample data reference

Mini retro prompts (after pilot ends)
- What surprised us about the data distribution or latency?
- Which metric most strongly correlated with business outcomes?
- What fallback prevented an incident?

Rough timeline (example 4-week plan)
- Week 0: kickoff, sample data ingest, smoke tests
- Week 1: baseline runs, initial evaluation on 50 examples, tweak prompts/model choice
- Week 2–3: larger run, instrumentation enabled, collect metrics
- Week 4: final evaluation, qualitative review, ROI summary, next steps

Open items for internal follow-up (for Asha / Lina / Jonah)
- Build a short pilot one-pager template and a token calc sheet we can reuse across sellers (priority: high)
- Create a short Confluence checklist for Private/Dedicated presales network checks (priority: med)
- Reinforce with SE/AE playbook where to escalate compliance blockers

Random scratch notes (raw):
- Could add a tiny decision tree: "need <300ms p95? -> dedicated; need VPC -> private; constrained budget -> hosted + cache"
- Consider a 15-minute "pilot speedrun" checklist for very small proofs (1 day)

-- end of doc --
